name: Monitor external managers
summary: Every month each of about 124 external mandates is reviewed: the manager's report is collected, its return is reconciled with the custodian-based figure, the analyst updates a scorecard against the benchmark and checks compliance exceptions and organisational news, and the portfolio manager writes an assessment. Quarter ends add a manager meeting and about once a year each manager gets an operational due diligence refresh. Mandates that hit written criteria go on a watch list, where a deeper review can end in a termination or resize decision. The work is a steady load of copying data between systems and waiting for late reports, with judgment concentrated in a few watch list cases.

baseline.org_archetype: A provincial not-for-profit asset manager of about $79 billion with about 124 external managers after a 2020 roster cut from 200.
baseline.notes: Snapshot of 2021; 2020 had far more terminations because of the roster restructuring.

unit_of_work: one monthly review of one external mandate
trigger: Month end, with the manager's monthly report and the performance team's mandate returns.
end_state: The month's review is recorded with the mandate's watch status, or a termination or resize decision is approved and handed to the transition process.

volume.seasonality: Quarter-end months add manager meetings; operational refreshes cluster after managers' controls reports are issued in the first half of the year.

evidence.note: 124 external managers at end of 2020 (mgr2020); one review per mandate per month as in the organisation file.

roles.title: Senior analyst, manager research and operational due diligence

evidence.note: FTE from about 2.5 hours of analyst time per mandate-month on average across 124 mandates, including meeting notes and annual ODD refreshes. Loaded cost from the organisation file, which prices investment professionals from estimated total pay; the Job Bank NOC 11101 Toronto median of $41.60 an hour is base pay only.

roles.title: Director, external manager research and operational due diligence

evidence.note: Watch list decisions, ODD sign-offs and review of termination recommendations.

Steps show a public equity mandate; about 40% of external mandates assumed to be public equities. Loaded cost from the organisation file, which prices investment professionals from estimated total pay; the Job Bank NOC 11101 Toronto median of $41.60 an hour is base pay only.
Does the same portfolio manager steps for public market alternatives mandates (about 20%).

roles.title: Principal, global credit (private and public credit)

evidence.note: Does the same steps for credit mandates (about 20%).

roles.title: Portfolio manager, fixed income and money markets

evidence.note: Does the same steps for fixed income mandates (about 20%).
Return reconciliation per mandate; loaded cost from the organisation file built on Job Bank NOC 11101 Toronto wages (median $41.60 an hour).

systems.name: Manager research database and due diligence questionnaire library
Risk analytics system (third-party factor and stress models)
Investment data warehouse and business intelligence reports
Custodian portal (custody, accounting records, net asset value reports, cash and corporate action notices)
Market data terminals and vendor feeds (prices, indices, reference data)
Email, video calls and collaboration suite
Document management system and virtual data rooms
Order management, pre-trade compliance and investment book of record platform (vendor software as a service)

steps.name: Receive and file manager monthly report
steps.description: After month end the analyst collects the manager's monthly report, holdings and transactions from email or the manager's portal, saves them to the research database and ticks receipt in the monitoring tracker. Late reports are listed for a chase.

evidence.note: uwo: manager reports are part of the periodic review. Arrival 4 to 12 days after month end is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Chase late manager report
steps.description: The analyst emails the manager's client service contact for the missing report or holdings file and records the delay, since repeated late reporting counts as an administrative issue.

evidence.note: uwo treats failure to report information as an administrative problem needing action. Times tier C.

steps.name: Reconcile manager return to custodian-based return
steps.description: The performance analyst compares the return the manager reports with the return calculated from custodian records in the performance system for the month, gross and net of fees. Differences above the tolerance (for example 10 basis points) are investigated.

control.basis: Performance measurement controls: mandate returns used for client and board reporting are reconciled to an independent source

evidence.note: Common practice at asset owners; tolerance and break rate are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Investigate return difference
steps.description: The performance analyst traces the difference to pricing sources, cash flow timing, accruals or fee treatment, queries the manager and the custodian and records the explanation or a correction.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Update mandate monitoring scorecard
steps.description: The analyst refreshes the mandate scorecard: returns against benchmark over one month, quarter, one, three and five years, tracking error, information ratio, factor and style exposures from the risk system and top positions from holdings, copying figures from the performance system into the workbook.

error.defect_description: Wrong period or benchmark pasted into the scorecard.

evidence.note: Performance against benchmark over short and long periods is the core of monitoring (uwo); SFERS used quarter, one and three year results and peer ranks. Times tier C.

steps.name: Check guideline compliance log
steps.description: The analyst looks up the compliance exception log and the manager's guideline compliance certificate for the month to see whether any breach or open exception affects the mandate.

evidence.note: The organisation file links compliance exceptions to this process; exception rate tier C.

steps.name: Follow up guideline breach with manager
steps.description: The portfolio manager calls the manager about the breach, agrees how and when it will be corrected and whether the client must be compensated, and confirms the fix with compliance.

control.basis: Investment compliance policy: every confirmed mandate breach has an agreed remediation and is reported

evidence.note: Author's estimate; detail of breach handling sits in investment-compliance-monitoring.

steps.name: Check organisational news
steps.description: The analyst scans manager notifications, trade press and regulatory filings for departures of named portfolio managers, ownership changes, asset flows and regulatory actions, and notes anything material.

evidence.note: Organisational change is a review trigger in uwo; GFOA lists key personnel. Times tier C.

steps.name: Review mandate and write assessment
steps.description: The portfolio manager reads the scorecard, holdings changes, manager commentary and notes, judges whether results fit the manager's style and the market, and writes a short assessment. At quarter ends and when an annual operational review is due, further steps follow.

next.condition: scorecard error found, analyst corrects it

evidence.note: Monthly review by the asset class team with quarterly meetings follows the organisation file; uwo reviews every manager quarterly. Times tier C.

steps.name: Hold quarterly manager review meeting
steps.description: The portfolio manager and analyst hold the quarterly call or meeting with the manager's portfolio managers: attribution, positioning, outlook, team and business changes and any open issues.

evidence.note: uwo: staff meet each manager periodically and the consultant yearly. Quarterly cadence from the organisation file; times tier C.

steps.name: Write meeting note
steps.description: The analyst writes the meeting note with actions and any change in conviction and files it in the research database for the quarterly client and board reporting.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Request annual operational due diligence update
steps.description: The analyst sends the manager the annual update questionnaire and document request: latest controls report (SOC 1) and bridge letter, audited financial statements, compliance attestations, insurance, business continuity test results and changes in service providers.

evidence.note: sbai2024: only 7% monitor managers less than annually; GFOA asks for at least annual due diligence reviews. Times tier C.

steps.name: Wait for manager's operational update
steps.description: The manager's operations and compliance staff complete the update and send the documents, often after their own audit cycle produces the controls report.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of response time.

steps.name: Review operational update and rerate
steps.description: The analyst reviews the responses and documents, reads exceptions in the controls report, compares them with last year's findings, holds a call with the chief operating officer if something changed, and proposes an updated operational rating.

error.defect_description: A control exception in the SOC report is overlooked.

evidence.note: Standard DDQ modules and risk-based ODD monitoring. Times tier C.

steps.name: Sign off operational rating
steps.description: The head of manager research reads the analyst's update note and the controls report exceptions, approves or changes the proposed rating, and flags any downgrade so it feeds the watch list test.

control.basis: Operational due diligence policy: ratings approved by the head of manager research

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Test mandate against watch list criteria
steps.description: The analyst checks the mandate against the watch list criteria: trailing three-year excess return below the tolerance, tracking error outside its range, style drift, departure of key people, an operational downgrade or repeated breaches. Mandates already on the watch list get a fuller monthly review.

control.basis: Manager monitoring policy with written watch list criteria

next.condition: no trigger and not on watch

evidence.note: sers2026: evaluation list under a board monitoring policy with quantitative and qualitative triggers; SFERS used one and three year underperformance. Shares tier C (about 10 of 124 mandates on watch).

steps.name: Decide watch list placement
steps.description: The head of manager research reviews the trigger with the portfolio manager and decides whether to place the mandate on the watch list, recording the reasons and what would take it off.

evidence.note: Placement flags a mandate for greater review and is not itself proof of a problem (sers2026). Times and split tier C.

steps.name: Notify manager of watch status
steps.description: The portfolio manager tells the manager about the watch status and the specific concerns and asks for a written plan or explanation before the next review.

evidence.note: uwo: a meeting is arranged and the manager is told the board's specific concerns. Times tier C.

steps.name: Run watch list review
steps.description: The portfolio manager and analyst examine attribution, style consistency, team changes and the manager's plan, meet the manager if needed and recommend keeping the mandate on watch, removing it, reducing its size or terminating it. Withholding new cash is a common interim step.

evidence.note: uwo lists withholding cash flows, reducing weight, reviewing termination terms and a replacement search; SFERS cut allocations while keeping contracts. Rates tier C.

steps.name: Draft termination or resize recommendation
steps.description: The portfolio manager writes the recommendation: evidence, reallocation target (internal strategy, another manager or a new search), notice terms in the agreement and a first estimate of transition cost.

evidence.note: uwo: identify notice period and termination clauses and estimate the costs of changing managers. Times tier C.

steps.name: Review recommendation
steps.description: The head of manager research reviews the recommendation with the asset class managing director and either sends it to the CIO or keeps the mandate on watch for another period.

next.condition: kept on watch for another period

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Approve termination or resize
steps.description: The CIO approves the termination or resize, or takes it to the investment committee when the reallocation is large; the decision then starts the termination and transition process.

control.basis: Delegated authority: terminating or resizing an external mandate needs CIO approval

evidence.note: Approval level is an assumption; the organisation file routes the decision to ext-manager-termination-transition.

steps.name: Record review conclusion
steps.description: The analyst records the month's conclusion, watch status and any actions in the research database and the roster dashboard used for quarterly client reports and the annual plan.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Return break with custodian figure
exceptions.description: The manager's reported return differs from the custodian-based return beyond tolerance, usually from pricing sources, accrual or cash flow timing.

exceptions.name: Late manager report
exceptions.description: The report or holdings file is missing at the cut-off and is chased.

exceptions.name: Guideline breach
exceptions.description: An open compliance exception needs the portfolio manager to agree remediation with the manager.

exceptions.name: Termination or resize
exceptions.description: A watch list mandate is recommended for termination or a smaller allocation and the CIO approves.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from month end to the review being recorded
benchmarks.population: Monthly external mandate reviews at Canadian public asset owners (author's estimate)

evidence.note: Manager reports and custodian-based returns arrive one to three weeks after month end; reviews are usually closed within the following month, longer at quarter ends. uwo shows the quarterly review cycle.

pain_points.description: Analysts copy returns, risk figures and holdings from the performance and risk systems into spreadsheet scorecards for every mandate every month.

evidence.note: Typical of the period's tools; the organisation file lists spreadsheets alongside a data warehouse.

pain_points.description: Reviews wait on late manager reports and on custodian-based returns, which arrive one to three weeks after month end.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Annual operational refreshes across more than 100 managers compete with new-manager due diligence for the same analysts; 41% of ODD professionals say they lack time to complete reviews.
Watch list decisions are slow and managers can stay on watch for several quarters before a decision.

evidence.note: Evaluation lists carry managers across quarters; time on watch is tier C.

sources.title: Selecting, Reviewing and Replacing Managers
sources.supports: Canadian pension board practice: quarterly review of each manager's short and long term performance against a market benchmark with consultant attribution and manager quarterly reports; staff meet each manager periodically and the consultant meets each manager every year; consultant ratings HIRE, RETAIN, REVIEW, TERMINATE; a downgrade to REVIEW triggers a meeting with the manager; responses to continued underperformance include withholding cash flows, reducing weight, reviewing notice periods and termination clauses, a replacement search and termination once a replacement is chosen; administrative problems (late reporting, inaccurate accounting) handled separately; benchmarks reassessed annually.

sources.title: Public Benefit Plan Investment Manager Evaluation List (as of March 31, 2026)
sources.publisher: RVK, Inc. and Pennsylvania SERS Investment Office (memo to the SERS Investment Committee)
sources.supports: Quarterly evaluation list compiled by the consultant and investment office under a board-adopted Investment Manager Monitoring Policy (2014, amended 2016 and 2022); placement flags quantitative or qualitative pattern changes for greater review and is not by itself evidence of a problem; two managers on the list for performance, one recommended for termination.

sources.title: Three Managers Put Under Review By San Francisco Pension Plan
sources.supports: Staff added three international equity strategies to the managers-under-review list for underperformance over the quarter and trailing one- and three-year periods and weak peer rankings; managers on the list receive in-depth monitoring and are subject to termination; allocations were reduced while contracts stayed in place.

sources.title: SBAI 2024 Operational Due Diligence Practices Survey
sources.supports: 70% of responding institutional investors have dedicated ODD teams, 80% of which report outside the investment function; 77% do a full ODD review at the start of a new manager relationship; 60% conduct onsite reviews for new managers and 7% do not; results go to the investment committee alone for 50%; 32% of ODD teams have a formal veto, used rarely or at most once a year by 73% of those; only 7% monitor managers less than annually, with a trend to risk-based monitoring; 59% use bespoke DDQs; 41% say they do not always have enough time to complete an ODD review; for private markets ODD is often embedded in the investment team's due diligence.

sources.title: Selecting Third-Party Investment Professionals for Pension Fund Assets (best practice)
sources.supports: Competitive, merit-based selection run by a consultant or review committee; candidate sources (consultant databases, references from other plans); conflict disclosure; RFP evaluation criteria (organisational, financial, investment, fee, operational); review of track record over 3, 5 and 10 years, risk management, back office and SOC 2 type reports; references from other pension clients and a presentation by the decision makers; management agreement terms; at least annual due diligence review of policy compliance and performance.

sources.title: Due Diligence Questionnaires (2019)
sources.supports: AIMA Illustrative Questionnaire for the Due Diligence of Investment Managers with modules for overview, governance, operations and risk management and fund terms, plus strategy modules (hedge fund, private credit, private equity) and topic modules (responsible investment, cyber security, outsourcing). Investors use it as an early step that guides further questions; standard questions let investors compare responses from several managers like for like.

sources.title: The model manager posts solid 2020 return, meets benchmark index (news release)
sources.publisher: The model manager via Cision Newswire
sources.supports: External manager roster cut from 200 to 124 in 2020, fund-of-funds eliminated, new strategic partnerships; $10 million of investment management fees saved; 2020 private commitments: three mid-market buyout fund commitments totalling $1 billion, real estate funds (KingSett Affordable Housing, Breakthrough Life Science, Dermody Industrial III), credit funds (Sagard Credit Partners II, Oaktree Opportunities XI).

sources.title: Wages: Financial Analyst near Toronto (ON), NOC 11101
sources.supports: Toronto region hourly wages low $27.97, median $41.60, high $73.57 (reference period 2023-2024).

assumptions: Steps show a public equity mandate reviewed by pm_public_equities; mandates in public market alternatives, credit and fixed income follow the same steps with pm_pma, pm_global_credit and pm_fixed_income, and FTE is split by an assumed share of mandates (40/20/20/20).
One case is one mandate-month. A quarter-end month (33% of cases) adds the manager meeting; about one case in twelve includes the annual operational refresh, so each manager gets one a year.

About 10 of 124 mandates (8%) are on the watch list at any time, about 2% of mandate-months hit a new trigger, and about 1% end in a termination or resize decision (roughly 1 to 1.5 a month), consistent with the organisation file's 0.5 to 6 terminations a month in steady state.
Trigger shares are allocations of the same monthly case to the objects that start it (manager report, performance results, compliance exceptions, new mandates), not separate cases.
Return reconciliation is shown as a monitoring step done by a performance analyst; the full performance calculation sits in performance-attribution.

Hands-on time of about 5 hours per mandate-month on average (about 3 hours in an ordinary month, more at quarter ends and in operational refresh months) is the author's estimate; with 124 mandates this is about 5 FTE spread over four research analysts, fifteen portfolio managers and the performance team.

The research analysts' implied load here (about 2.5 FTE) plus searches (about 1 FTE), onboarding and terminations exceeds the four analysts in the organisation file; stated FTE is held at 2.0 on the assumption that asset class analysts update some scorecards and ordinary-month reviews are sometimes lighter than modelled. The research team in the organisation file may be small for 124 mandates.
Loaded costs come from the organisation file.
